title: Cold-induced structural remodeling of the translation machinery in a thermophilic eukaryote
projectDescription: During protein synthesis, ribosomes iteratively cycle through multiple functional states, accompanied by large-scale conformational rearrangements, translocation of transfer RNAs through the intersubunit space, and binding and dissociation of translation elongation factors. In vitro and in situ structural biology approaches have been used to characterize different structural states of the ribosome and their relative abundance within the translation elongation cycle, providing a comprehensive picture of the translational landscape in mesophilic organisms. Here, we investigated adaptations of the translation process to life at high temperatures and characterized how thermophilic cells respond to cold stress at the level of the translation machinery. We used cellular cryo-electron tomography to visualize the translation machinery in the thermophilic eukaryote Chaetomium thermophilum, natively growing at 50 - 55°C. Comparison to published data indicated that the overall distribution of translation elongation cycle states in mesophilic and thermophilic eukaryotes was comparable, demonstrating that the translational landscape is deeply conserved across a vast range of physiological temperatures. Under cold stress, we observed re-equilibration in the relative abundance of translation elongation cycle states accompanied by elevated eIF5A association to ribosomes and a strong enrichment of eEF2-bound hibernating ribosomes, reflecting an altered translational landscape and partial shutdown of translational activity in response to suboptimal growth temperatures. Remarkable cell-to-cell variation in the translational landscape and its remodeling under cold stress suggests striking flexibility at the level of protein synthesis. Collectively, this study provides a molecular resolution view on translation in a thermophilic organism and how it is remodeled in response to cold stress on a single-cell level.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Protein samples (≤20 µg) were prepared for digestion using the Single Tube Solid Phase Sample Preparation (SP3) method on a KingFisher Apex (Thermo Fisher Scientific) platform as described before [cite: PMID: 41590846]. After digestion, peptides were desalted using Affinisep Stage Tips 200µl C18 T2. After initial sequential washing with (i) 50% MeOH, (ii) 80% ACN, 0.1% TFA, and (iii) 0.1% TFA, acidified peptides were loaded on the stage tips. After washing with 0.1% TFA, peptides were eluted twice using 80% ACN, 0.1% TFA [cite: PMID: 17703201]. Nanoflow LC-MS2 analysis was performed using the Vanquish Neo coupled to an Orbitrap Eclipse (Thermo Fisher Scientific) as described before [cite: PMID: 40846850]. Peptide separation was achieved using a 120-minute linear gradient, starting at 4% solvent B and gradually increasing to 32% over the first 100 minutes, followed by a further increase to 49% over the next 20 minutes, and finally a wash step with 99% solvent B. The Orbitrap Tribrid Eclipse was operated in data-independent acquisition (DIA) mode. Full scan precursor spectra were acquired in the centroid mode with 60k resolution, AGC target = 1.2e6, MaxIT = Auto, RF Lens = 30%, mass range = 400–920. Fragment spectra were then recorded using centroid mode at 30.000 resolution, fragmenting 40 variable windows covering the entire precursor mass range, designed to balance precursor density and minimize spectral complexity. Isolated precursors were fragmented in the HCD cell using 27% normalized collision energy, a normalized AGC target of 1e6, and a maxIT of 54 ms.
dataProcessingProtocol: The MS/MS spectra were searched against the C. thermophilum (downloaded May 2026, UP000008066), and a built-in contaminant database using DIA-NN 2.2.0. [cite: PMID: 31768060]. A maximum of 1 missed cleavage and 2 variable modifications were allowed. The fragment ion mass tolerance was set to 20 ppm, and the parent ion mass tolerance to 10 ppm. The match between runs option was enabled, together with protein inference, and the following settings were used: Scoring = "Generic", Proteotypicity = ‘Protein names’, Machine learning = ‘NNs cross-validated’, Cross-run normalization = ‘Off’, Library Generation = ‘IDs, RT and IM Profiling’ and Speed and RAM usage = ‘Optimal results’. Precursor FDR was set to 1%. Trypsin was specified as an enzyme. The following variable modifications were allowed: Oxidation (M), Met-loss (M), whereas Carbamidomethylation (C) was set as a fixed modification. Quantification was done using DIA-NN's built-in algorithm QuantUMS (high precision) [cite PMID: 42204360].
